title: Smallest angle of minimum deviation of a thin prism whose refractive index varies with wavelength
summary: A thin 6 deg prism with n = alpha lambda + beta/lambda^2: rotate it to find the minimum deviation, scan the wavelength, and find where Dm is smallest. lambda_min = (2 beta/alpha)^(1/3) = 0.4 um, n = 1.8, Dm = 4.8 deg - option B.
subject: Physics
topic: Minimum deviation of a thin prism with a wavelength-dependent index - the wavelength deviated least
subtopics: Angle of minimum deviation: the symmetric path through a prism
Thin prism: Dm = (n - 1)A; exact: n = sin((A + Dm)/2)/sin(A/2)
Dispersion: refractive index as a function of wavelength
Minimising n(lambda) = alpha lambda + beta/lambda^2 by calculus
concepts: For a thin prism Dm = (n - 1)A, so the smallest Dm across wavelengths is at the smallest n(lambda)
dn/dlambda = alpha - 2 beta/lambda^3 = 0 gives lambda_min = (2 beta/alpha)^(1/3) = 0.4 um; n'' > 0 so it is a minimum
n(0.4) = 1.2 + 0.6 = 1.8, so Dm = 0.8 x 6 = 4.8 deg - option B; the exact prism formula gives 4.81 deg
Options C (3.2) and D (2.4) need n = 1.53 and 1.4, below the material's minimum 1.8; option A (6.4) needs n = 2.07, reached only at 0.28 and 0.6 um
Minimum deviation is found experimentally by rotating the prism: the deviation dips to its least value on the symmetric path

methods: MathonGo solution (their Q21 = Physics Q.3) read first as the conceptual reference; its answer (B) agrees
Independent solve: lambda^3 = 2 beta/alpha = 0.064, lambda = 0.4 um, n = 1.8, Dm = (n - 1)A = 4.8 deg
Exact rational arithmetic: lambda_min = 0.4 um exactly, n = 1.8, thin-prism Dm = 4.8 deg
sympy: the only stationary point is 0.4 um, n'' > 0, n -> infinity at both ends (global minimum)
Exact prism formula: Dm = 2 asin(1.8 sin 3 deg) - 6 deg = 4.811 deg, nearest option B
Brute-force ray trace (1601 wavelengths x 6000 incidences): smallest Dm 4.811 deg at 0.400 um on the symmetric path
Options audited: C and D need n below 1.8; A needs n = 2.067, reached only at 0.280 and 0.600 um
